messages:
Sofia Martinez: Is it possible to remove a dependent mid-year if they got coverage elsewhere? My partner just started a new job and wants to add our kid to their plan.

Evan (People Ops): Yes, thats generally a qualifying life event: gain of other coverage. We'll need proof of the new coverage effective date.

Sofia Martinez: What proof exactly? An ID card? Enrollment confirmation?

Priya (Benefits): Acceptable proofs: 1) Insurance ID card showing effective date, 2) Carrier enrollment confirmation letter, 3) Employer benefits enrollment confirmation email with effective date. Screenshots ok if legible.

Sofia Martinez: If I remove my child, can I still use FSA funds for expenses already incurred?

Evan (People Ops): Yes, FSA reimbursements are based on expense date. If you paid for something while the child was covered, you can still submit for reimbursement as long as it's within the plans claim submission window.

Sofia Martinez: How long do I have to submit docs?

Priya (Benefits): Submit within 60 days of the QLE. Benefits@redwood.com subject: "QLE - Remove dependent - gain other coverage". We'll process and confirm effective dates and payroll changes.

Sofia Martinez: Thanks  sending the new employer enrollment confirmation now.

people-ops-bot: FYI: Open enrollment reminder - check dependent lists before Nov 15 to avoid surprises during Jan 1 effective date.
